fields.v: Routing: 75 core queries on Easy and Hard pools, averaged; configurations: encoders and encoder x reranker pipelines; baseline: strongest base pipeline Qwen3-8B x 8B; held constant: pool, queries, top-20 candidates, input caps. End-to-end: 4 models in Claude Code harness, 1200 s timeout, conditions no skill / gold / retrieved top-1 / top-10 from base vs SkillRouter, natural pool. Acceptance tests: SkillsBench success validation. Repetitions: 3 trials per task per condition (end-to-end); routing: one evaluation per configuration, no repetitions reported. Human intervention: none

rev.why: 'routing deterministic' is not stated in the text; the paper reports one routing evaluation per configuration and says nothing on determinism or seeds

fields.v: SkillRouter 1.2B Hit@1 74.0% vs 68.0% for 16B base (+6.0pp; +8.0 Easy, +4.0 Hard), 13x fewer parameters, 5.8x lower latency; base better on multi-skill FC@10 (.382 vs .353). Removing body drops Hit@1 by 37-44pp; oracle nd recovers part (6.7-21.3pp residual gap); nd-only fine-tuned encoder 14.0pp below all-field. Supp benchmark: .641 vs .637. End-to-end: +1.78pp (top-1) and +2.33pp (top-10) over base router; larger for Claude models (+3.22pp) than glm-5/Kimi (+0.89pp). No significance testing (stated)

Routing metrics distinguished configurations; end-to-end differences small and per-agent mixed. Repeatability: 3 trials end-to-end, no variance or tests reported. Limitations stated: 75-query core small; SkillBench-Supp LLM-generated (transfer check, not human validated); downstream four agents under one budget without significance testing; Hit@1 for multi-skill queries mechanical

Small core set; whether the body-access effect transfers to typed API repositories, vertical catalogs or multi-hop agentic retrieval is open; retrieval fails on tasks needing multi-hop prerequisite inference; compact router weaker in specialized multi-skill domains

Table 25 (per-agent) rebuilt from pdftotext column order; SkillRouter is worse than the base router for glm-5 top-1 (23.11 vs 24.89) and Kimi-K2.5 top-10 (18.22 vs 20.00), which the main text averages away. Hard tier uses LLM-generated distractors. Base models (Qwen3) and the authors are both Alibaba. No code, model or data release stated in the text read. No pre-registration.
